extracted.intended_audience: state agency staff, regulatory boards, and interested members of the public
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for designing and operating public participation (PPG) processes for Virginia state regulatory actions, and for members of the public wishing to participate (comment forums, hearings, petitions, advisory committees).

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirement to promulgate Public Participation Guidelines (PPGs)
rubrics_metrics.description: Section 2.2-4007.02 of the Code of Virginia requires all non-exempt agencies to promulgate public participation guidelines (PPGs).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Although called guidelines, PPGs are regulations by which every agency or board must abide. Agencies must prepare and publish PPGs to facilitate public involvement in the regulatory process.

rubrics_metrics.name: PPGs must set out methods for identifying and notifying interested persons
rubrics_metrics.description: PPGs must set out any methods for identifying and notifying people who might be interested in a regulatory action.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This includes any specific means for seeking input from interested persons or groups the board or agency intends to use in addition to the NOIRA.

rubrics_metrics.name: PPGs must describe additional means for seeking input beyond the NOIRA
rubrics_metrics.description: PPGs must set out any specific means for seeking input from interested persons or groups your board or agency intends to use in addition to the NOIRA.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agencies should specify the alternative or supplemental outreach and comment mechanisms they will use (e.g., forums, advisory panels, direct notices).

rubrics_metrics.name: PPGs must set out provisions for use of standing or ad hoc advisory panels and consultations
rubrics_metrics.description: PPGs must set out provisions for the use of standing or ad hoc advisory panels and consultation with groups and individuals who want to work with an agency to develop a regulatory action.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: PPGs must address the circumstances in which an agency considers a panel or consultation appropriate and intends to make use of a panel or consultation (i.e., policy for formation, membership, and when to employ panels).

rubrics_metrics.name: PPGs must include right to representation by counsel or other representative
rubrics_metrics.description: Chapter 795 of the 2012 Acts of Assembly added language allowing interested persons to be accompanied by and represented by counsel or other representative; this should be included in an agency's PPGs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agencies should incorporate this model language into their PPG documents to comply with statutory changes permitting representation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use DPB model PPGs as an example
rubrics_metrics.description: The guidance points agencies to the most updated model PPGs (DPBModelPPG2016.doc) as an example.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agencies can use the model PPGs as a template or reference when drafting their own binding PPGs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Make the regulatory process open and accessible via the Town Hall
rubrics_metrics.description: The Town Hall makes the regulatory process open and accessible to all Virginians; anyone with access to the Internet can view all aspects of the process and participate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Opening up the process increases transparency and lowers barriers for public viewing and participation in regulatory activities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Automatic email notification for registered public
rubrics_metrics.description: Any member of the public can register with the Town Hall and sign up to receive e-mail notification about regulatory actions and meetings related to agencies, boards, and regulations they are interested in.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A 'Meetings' email and a 'Regulatory Actions' email are sent nightly to registered users whose preferences match activities for that day; agencies should encourage registration and use notifications to inform stakeholders.

rubrics_metrics.name: Agency mailing lists to inform interested users
rubrics_metrics.description: State agency users can send out information concerning regulatory activities to specific users who have expressed interest in a specific Agency, Board or Chapter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For example, an agency may send out a summary of public comments and the agency's response at the conclusion of a public comment period. More detailed operational guidance is provided for state agency users.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public Comment Forums must permit online submission and viewing of comments
rubrics_metrics.description: Anyone may submit on-line comments for any open public comment forum and view those comments made by others.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Forums are held for NOIRA stages, Proposed stages, Final stages, Petitions for Rulemaking and Periodic Reviews. Forums open automatically upon the date the event is published in The Virginia Register; duration varies depending on event type.

rubrics_metrics.name: Forums are tied to publication in The Virginia Register; opening and durations vary
rubrics_metrics.description: Public comment forums open automatically upon the date the event is published in The Virginia Register. How long a forum is open varies depending on the event.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agencies should be aware of statutory or procedural timelines that determine forum openings and lengths and communicate those to potential commenters.

rubrics_metrics.name: Board meetings should be open and set aside time for public input
rubrics_metrics.description: As a general rule, all board meetings are open to the public; agencies are encouraged, if possible, to set aside time to receive input from the public during these meetings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Setting aside time in regular meetings encourages participation from members of the public who attend to become informed or to offer comments on regulations in development.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public hearings convened specifically to receive public comment
rubrics_metrics.description: A public hearing is a special type of meeting usually convened for the sole purpose of receiving public comment on a regulatory action.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Board members and/or agency staff are present to receive public comments; hearings should be listed appropriately on the Town Hall and conducted to facilitate receipt of comments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Petition for rulemaking must state substance and purpose and cite authority
rubrics_metrics.description: To qualify as a 'petition for rulemaking,' the communication must (1) state the substance and purpose of the regulatory action that is requested (including reference to any applicable VAC sections), and (2) reference the legal authority of the agency to take the action requested, per §2.2-4007(A) of the Code of Virginia.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agencies should follow the statutory steps for submitting and processing petitions; charts and more detailed process descriptions are provided to explain the petition process.

rubrics_metrics.name: Agencies may use ad hoc advisory committees/TACs to assist drafting
rubrics_metrics.description: Often an agency will put together a committee consisting of regulants, advocacy groups, and other concerned citizens to assist the board in drafting or amending a regulation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: PPGs must set out a general policy for use of standing or ad hoc advisory panels and explain when such committees are appropriate and how they will be used in the regulatory development process.

rubrics_metrics.name: Best practice: seek input early (at or before the NOIRA stage)
rubrics_metrics.description: By seeking input from people with different perspectives on a regulation at or before the NOIRA stage (and before drafting the regulation), the agency will be more fully aware of the issues and evidence supporting various approaches.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Early input improves the quality of regulations by identifying ambiguities, omissions, unintended consequences, and other problems that may otherwise be overlooked, and helps agencies make better choices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Best practice: communicate with concerned parties before publication to avoid controversy
rubrics_metrics.description: It is best to avoid a situation where significant opposition and controversy are generated upon the publication of a regulatory action; by communicating with concerned parties before publication, agencies can gauge reaction and help to avoid problems from developing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proactive outreach can reduce post-publication opposition and streamline implementation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Best practice: respond meaningfully to input to build support and compliance
rubrics_metrics.description: Actively seeking input from the public and responding in a meaningful fashion will reap dividends in the form of greater trust, an enhanced reputation, support for the regulatory action, and compliance once implemented.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Documenting how public input influenced decisions (e.g., summaries and agency responses) can increase legitimacy and acceptance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Best practice: educate regulants in advance to minimize surprise at implementation
rubrics_metrics.description: Educating regulants in advance of implementation will help to minimize surprise on the part of the regulated community.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Advance education (through outreach, notices, summaries) eases transition and implementation of new regulations and reduces resistance.
